maya: Heads up — we got an ECC spike in us-west-gpu pool around 2026-03-17T12:14Z. Alert showed corrected ECC errors jumping on nodes gpu-node-07..10 and I see some recurring Xid 31 on node-09. Posting raw alert: `ERR: nv_gpu_ecc_corrected > 0 (sustained)`

raj: saw that. Prom query?

maya: `increase(nv_gpu_ecc_corrected_total{region=\"us-west\"}[1h])` shows ~620 on node-09, ~180 on node-07, 90 on node-08. Xid 31 counts: `increase(nv_gpu_xid_errors_total[10m])` -> node-09 = 3 in 10m.

lin: quick context — our current auto-drain logic is: soft threshold = 500 corrected / 1h -> add tag `needs-inspect`; hard threshold = 1500 corrected / 1h or any Xid >= 10 -> auto-drain and replace. Right?

maya: yes, that's what's running in prod right now for hosted pools. But dedicated pools have auto-drain disabled.

dana: node-09 also had a short network flakiness earlier (kube-proxy conn reset) — could be correlated. Any IO/PCIe errors in dmesg?

maya: pulling dmesg from node-09: ```Mar 17 12:09:34 kernel: NVRM: Xid (31): GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 17 12:09:40 kernel: mdev: pci_bus_read_config_word failed
Mar 17 12:10:05 kernel: NVRM: RmVfPutInstance: bad vgpu instance```

raj: Xid 31 = gpu fell off bus — usually bad PCIe or power. Historically those nodes either needed reseating or replacement.

lin: we should not hard-drain immediately. Proposal: change thresholds to be more conservative for multi-tenant hosted: soft-inspect at 200 corrected / 30m, escalates to hard-drain at 1200 / 1h OR Xid >= 5 within 15m. Add a 10m cooldown window so we don't oscillate.

maya: +1 for cooldown. Also suggest marking nodes with label `gpu.flaky=true` when they hit soft-inspect so autoscaler avoids packing new long-running jobs.

dana: ops question — if we lower thresholds, we increase churn and replacement costs. Need to quantify: how many replacements per month at new threshold vs today. Can infra finance run a quick estimate? cc @finance but we can approximate: current replacement rate is ~3/month; this change might double it during seasonal spike.

raj: consequences for customer SLAs: for Dedicated customers we must opt-out of auto-drain. For hosted pools we can be more aggressive but prefer `soft-inspect` first so low-latency jobs keep running.

lin: action items I propose:
- Change alert rule: `nv_gpu_ecc_corrected_total` increase window -> 30m for soft, 1h for hard.
- Implement label `gpu.flaky=true` and a scheduler taint with `PreferNoSchedule` for long jobs (batch still allowed).
- Auto-drain policy: hard triggers only if Xid >= 5 OR corrected > 1200/1h. Include 10m cooldown and require oncall confirmation before replacement if node has <50% pod disruption budget impact.
- Add new Grafana dashboard panel for per-node ECC trending with small-multiples.

maya: also add an ephemeral runbook snippet in the alert: quick checks (prom queries, dmesg, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.free,utilization.gpu --format=csv -i <id>`, extract card ID `lspci -v | grep -i nvidia`), then `kubectl cordon` -> `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` if proceeding.

dana: here's a proto alert text we can use: "GPU ECC spike ({{ $labels.instance }}): corrected errors {{ $value }} in {{ $labels.window }}, Xid count {{ $labels.xids }}. Actions: run quick checks, set gpu.flaky label if >=soft threshold, escalate to hard-drain if hard threshold reached."

raj: one safety check — for nodes attached to Dedicated pools we must bypass auto-drain and instead create an automated incident to infra-ops for manual handling.

lin: we can wire that by checking labels: `pool=dedi-*` in the Prom rule. If pool matches, alert severity = P2 and send to #infra-ops but don't trigger drain workflow.

maya: vote?

lin: +1

raj: +1
dana: +0 (need cost estimate)

maya: ok consensus. I'll open an ops RFC and a PR for the alert rules and the scheduler change. Target: roll to staging tomorrow, canary to us-west with 2 nodes, then global.

maya: PR checklist items: include unit tests for cooldown logic, test that dedicated pools have auto-drain disabled, add note in oncall runbook, update playbook doc with `card-respin` vs `replace` decision tree.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: Created issue INFRA-4678: "ECC surge triage & auto-drain policy update" assigned to maya. ETA 2026-03-20.
